story.head: The Stars’ power play has a target
paras: The Stars won the teams’ first meeting this season, 3-2 in overtime in Dallas on Oct 22. The Stars (9-5-2) lost 2-1 in a shootout to Columbus on Nov 5. The Jets have won two in a row, the last a 6-2 rout of Vancouver. This is a Central Division matchup, with the Jets seventh (tied for 24th in the NHL) and the Stars third (tied for 11th).
This season, the Stars have outscored teams 44-36, but only 29-26 at 5-on-5. On special teams, they’ve outscored teams 9-5, and no team creates more chances on the power play.

The Jets rarely ice the puck (4th), but don't block many shots (29th). They also create more chances on the penalty kill than almost anyone (2nd), and that sets up a fight with the Stars’ power play (1st), which could do real damage against the Jets’ penalty kill (29th). The Stars play slow, tight games (lowest) and have the league’s most dangerous power play (1st). They also block more shots than anyone (1st), and the Jets’ knack for getting shots through meets a team that blocks a lot. Dallas has allowed 2.25 goals a game, the second fewest in the league.

Kyle Connor (13 G / 6 A / 19 P in 17 GP) leads the Jets in scoring, with seven points in his last five games and eight goals in 13 games against Dallas since 2023-24. Mark Scheifele (3 G / 13 A / 16 P in 17 GP) isn’t far behind, with eight points in his last five games. For the Stars, Mikko Rantanen (9 G / 10 A / 19 P in 16 GP) leads the way in scoring, with a point in five straight games against Winnipeg. Jason Robertson (8 G / 10 A / 18 P in 16 GP) is next in line.

Stuart Skinner (5-4-3 / .885 SV% in 12 GS) is in line to start for Winnipeg. Jake Oettinger (8-3-1 / .910 SV% in 12 GS) has been outstanding for Dallas and will likely start. Skinner has a .850 save percentage in eight starts against the Stars, well under his usual .899. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.
The Stars usually control more of the chances than the Jets do.
